newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia prepared to lift diplomat's immunity.
newsitem.headline: Georgia prepared to lift diplomat's immunity.

text.p: Georgian leader Eduard Shevardnadze said on Friday he was prepared to waive the diplomatic immunity of a Georgian diplomat involved in a five-car crash in which a teenage girl was killed.

A written statement by Shevardnadze also said the diplomat, Georgy Makharadze, should stay in the United States until an investigation into the accident was completed "unless a different agreement between the two governments is reached".
Shevardnadze had received the U.S. charge d'affaires in Tbilisi Lawrence Kerr and reaffirmed his commitment to cooperate in an investigation, a later statement said.

"The President said that an impartial investigation and establishing the truth are important to him, not only in view of international conventions and obligations, but primarily in terms of moral principle," it said.

It said Kerr had reported that Makharadze, 35, had tried to leave the United States after last Friday's incident, in which the car he was driving started a five-vehicle collision in Washington. A Brazilian teenager died in the crash.
Shevardnadze told Kerr he knew nothing of Makharadze's attempt to flee the country and expressed his concern over the accident, the presidential office said.

"The president of Georgia is prepared to waive the diplomatic immunity of Georgy Makharadze. Makharadze shall remain in the United States of America until the completion of the investigation and legal procedures unless a different agreement between the two governments is reached," they said.
Shevardnadze, a former Soviet foreign minister who played a major role in ending the Cold War, is clearly keen to maintain good relations with Washington.
The U.S. State Department which on Thursday formally asked Georgia to waive Makharadze's immunity, welcomed Shevardnadze's announcement as a "courageous step".
But U.S. officials said in Washington that the statement did not amount to lifting the diplomat's immunity and that Georgia would have to do that if the U.S. authorities decided to bring charges.
